heading: ## Acceptance criteria
markdown:
- With the board up on Linux and nothing happening, it redraws once a second: the lockup alternates between its two frames and the header's `up` clock advances every second. A single wait slice never blocks longer than `status::POLL`, and a file landing in the queue or commands directory still ends the wait early.

A failure from any other key reaches the reader under the board instead of being discarded, and one interrupted read no longer stops the board reading keys for the rest of the loop iteration.

The section to add, verbatim:

    ## The upgrade suite

    `scripts/e2e/suites/upgrade.sh` asks one question, and it is the only suite that asks it: does
    this binary still read what an older one wrote? Its fixtures are whole `.spoolway/` trees under
    `scripts/e2e/fixtures/`, one per released version, each scaffolded by the binary of that
    version. The suite copies one, runs `spoolway update` over the copy, and says what survived.

    It is in the `nightly` tier and not in `pr`, and that is the only place this project's two tiers
    differ. So the `suite` step never runs it, it cannot send a task back to you, and it costs the
    per-task flow nothing. What runs it is the daily scheduled run on main and the release workflow,
    which is the last point a migration break can still be caught cheaply.

    That is also why this is the one suite you may run yourself. `scripts/e2e/run.sh --suite upgrade`
    runs it alone and takes seconds, because the fixtures are already on disk and no old binary is
    built at run time. Run it when your change touches a config key, a pipeline key, a generated block
    or the prompt layout, and skip it otherwise — nothing downstream of you will run it in time to
    help.

    Every other suite asserts against a system this same commit built. This one asserts against files
    nobody will ever touch again, so it goes stale on its own, and it is the first suite to fail when
    any of those four things move. That failure is the suite working. Three shapes it takes:

    - **A config key was retired or renamed.** The old spelling is still in every fixture that had it.
      What has to carry it across is `Config::migrate` in `src/config.rs`, and a missing arm there is
      the defect. Fix the migration, not the fixture.
    - **A generated block changed shape.** The command `spoolway update` swaps that one region and
      copies every byte around it through unread. Assert that the prose around the block came back
      unchanged, because that is the promise it would break.
    - **A released version has no fixture.** Somebody cut a release without adding one. Say so in your
      handoff; do not scaffold a fixture yourself, since only that version's own binary can write one.

    A fixture is a record of what an old version wrote. Editing one to reach green destroys the record
    and the suite stops testing anything.

heading: ## Context

That handle is line-buffered, so one frame reaches the terminal as many writes, and the terminal can paint the blank or half-drawn screen between them. On WSL, inside Herdr, this shows as flicker.

heading: ## Acceptance criteria
markdown:
- The writer sends one frame as exactly one call to `write` on its output, followed by a flush. The bytes are `ESC[?2026h ESC[H`, then each row followed by `ESC[K` and `\n`, then `ESC[J ESC[?2026l`. A row whose visible width equals the pane width gets no `ESC[K`. Visible width is counted with escape codes left out, the same way the screens already measure a row.
- The writer takes the pane size as an argument. It writes nothing when both the rows and the pane size equal the last frame it wrote. A `forget` call clears its memory of the last frame, so the next frame is always written.
- Leaving the screen, both on a normal exit and from the panic hook in `src/platform.rs`, writes `ESC[?2026l` immediately before `ESC[?1007h ESC[?1049l`, and still writes that sequence only once.
- `vt100` is added under a new `[dev-dependencies]` section, and nowhere else. The test module holds a frozen copy of today's write (erase, then one `writeln!` per row) that only tests call. Tests play old and new output into a `vt100` screen and require the same contents cell for cell, in text, colour and bold. They cover an ordinary frame, a full-width row, a shorter frame after a longer one, and one frame after a completely different one.
- Tests with a counting writer show one frame is one write call, an unchanged frame writes nothing, the same rows at a new pane size write, and a frame after `forget` writes. End-to-end coverage: none in this task, because no screen calls the writer yet. The task `frames-onto-writer` carries it into the suites.

heading: ## Context
markdown:
- `models.<glob>.slots` caps how many lanes run one model at once, and `start_lanes` in `src/dispatch.rs` fills that cap by counting only the lanes spoolway itself started — a subagent spawned inside a lane's prompt and a session a person opens in another terminal are both invisible to it.
- That cap describes what one graphics card holds, so a count that sees only spoolway's own work is a cap that can be exceeded without anything noticing or reporting it.
- The decision this task implements: a model declares itself local with a new `local = true` key, and when a queued task routes to one the board carries a standing line asking the person not to start their own sessions on that card.
- The line is information and never a gate — the run always starts, there is no dialog, no abort, no "don't ask again" and no off switch of any kind.
- Nothing about how lanes are counted changes. The line is what is paid instead of a truthful count, and it is deliberately not a fix for the undercount.

heading: ## Context
markdown:
- Everybody upgrading from 0.2 has a home filed under their checkout's basename,
  holding a queue, an archive, a ledger and dispatched worktrees. Nothing in the new
  scheme addresses it, so without this they open spoolway to an empty queue.
- After `binding-record`, a legacy home is not a special shape. Its `project.toml`
  carries a `root` and no `id`, which is one more row for the same table to answer.
- A home holds two things that record their own absolute path: the dispatcher's lock
  at `dispatch.pid`, and the git worktrees cut under it, which git records a path for
  in the main checkout's own bookkeeping.
- `Lock::holder` at `src/lock.rs:129` already tests both the pid and its start time,
  so a dispatcher that crashed reads as no dispatcher and cannot wedge this forever.
- Every state file is addressed through `Repo::home()` at `src/repo.rs:231`, which is
  what makes moving the directory once enough to carry all of it.

heading: ## Acceptance criteria
markdown:
- The first command that resolves a home moves a legacy home to `~/.spoolway/<label>-<id>/`
  and prints one line naming both paths and what came across, and no later command
  moves anything again.
- The move is refused while `Lock::holder` reports a live dispatcher or any worktree
  under the home is checked out, naming the old path in full and leaving it untouched,
  and the same command succeeds once the run has finished.
- A `git worktree repair` pass runs after a successful move, so worktrees that were not
  live enough to block it still resolve from the main checkout afterwards.
- A clone that has both a legacy home and a home under its id refuses and names both
  directories rather than merging or picking one.
- Two commands racing on the first run after an upgrade leave exactly one moved home
  and no error, whichever of them gets there first.

It reuses `src/lock.rs`'s pid liveness and staleness reaping, is never held across a multiplexer call, and `unqueue_task` takes it too rather than renaming over a newer pending document.

heading: ## Context
markdown:
Three to five facts, one line each.

- The board's `p` key takes three roads today, in `Board::begin_pause_cursor` in `src/status/mod.rs`: a task with a live agent lane is interrupted and parked with no confirmation, a task on a running command step opens `BoardMode::ConfirmPause`, and every other state is a silent no-op.
- `P` (`begin_pause_all`) parks every live agent lane *before* its panel opens, so answering `esc` cancels only the half of the pause that had not happened yet.
- The decision this task implements: `p` and `P` always park, and the only thing that varies is whether a confirm panel opens first — it opens exactly when something is live for that scope, and it names what pausing would cut short.
- Two readers answer half the question each and neither is shaped for the panel: `live_agent_lane_tasks` returns indices into a task slice, `running_command_steps` returns records for the whole queue at once.
- `paused` and `blocked` are already stopped and already waiting on a person, and an archived `done` row is not in the queue directory `repo.tasks()` reads, so all three are no-ops for `p` rather than states to park.

heading: ## Acceptance criteria
markdown:
- `p` on a row with no live agent lane and no running command step parks the task on `paused` with no panel, from `queued`, from a quota-parked row, and from a row sitting on a real step between two lanes.
- `p` on a row whose agent lane is live, and `p` on a row whose command run is in flight, both open a confirm panel naming the step, its kind and its elapsed time, and neither writes a task file or interrupts anything until the panel is answered.
- `enter` on either pause panel carries out the pause — the lane interrupted through `Mux::interrupt_lane`, or the command run stopped through `Runs::stop` — and parks the task; `esc` leaves the task, the lane and the run exactly as they were.
- `P` with anything live in the run opens one panel listing every abort plus a count of the tasks that would pause with nothing interrupted, writes nothing until it is answered, and with nothing live anywhere parks every eligible task with no panel.
- `p` and `P` are no-ops on a `paused` row, a `blocked` row and an archived `done` row.
- Any key on either pause panel other than `enter` or `esc` is ignored and leaves the panel open.
- End-to-end coverage: extend the board-key coverage under `scripts/e2e/` that already drives `p` and `P`, so a pause from a state with nothing live and a pause that answers a panel are both exercised against the built binary.

- Appending to the ledger takes a file lock, so two `spoolway` commands banking the same session at the same time cannot both append the same delta and double-count an interactive session's cost.
- No lane record is removed before its usage is banked. `clean_up` banks the way `sweep_on_stop` already does, the headless pause path banks the interrupted turn before `stop_lane` removes the record, and a lane held for a person banks the delta a person's own rounds in that pane added when it is finally freed.
- The ledger is read once per invocation. `sweep` builds the per-session banked map in a single pass and hands it down; the dispatcher's ceiling checks, `carried_session`, `readopted` and `lane_session` all answer from one per-pass read; `elsewhere` checks a file's existence and size instead of parsing every other project's ledger to print a one-line hint.
- Banked totals and transcript segments are keyed the same way, so a skill named `plan` is banked once rather than in full on every command. Readers that need only the last record — `last_turn_aborted_in` and `last_turn_at` — stream or seek rather than loading a whole transcript into a `Vec<serde_json::Value>`.
- The reporting surfaces stop losing data: the cache checks more than byte length before serving a prefix, CSV exports quote a field holding a comma, quote or newline, `eval --json` carries `project` on skill rows as it already does on pipeline rows, the eval export cannot silently overwrite a file exported in the same minute, run and session ids do not fall back to clock and pid where `/dev/urandom` is absent, and the `live_session` transcript cache drops entries whose lane is gone.

End-to-end coverage: none, and why — the only usage-facing suite is
`scripts/e2e/suites/warmth.sh`, which spends real money against a cloud model
and is the wrong place to prove banking arithmetic. These cases belong in the
unit tests already in `src/usage.rs`, including one that runs two banks
concurrently.

heading: ## Context
markdown:
Three to five facts, one line each. The plan that produced this task is not
something you can read, so this is where its ground goes: what the surrounding
system does today, the decision this task implements, and the constraint that makes
the obvious approach wrong. Facts and names, not argument.

- `spoolway agent verify <kind> --live` runs one real turn of an agent in a scratch git repo, to check the launch and accounting contract against the real binary.
- For a kind that pins its session by home rather than by id, `agent_verify_live` calls `crate::agent::prepare_session_home` and hands the resulting directory to a `ScratchTree` guard.
- `ScratchTree::drop` removes both the scratch repo and that home, so the rollout the live turn just wrote is deleted on the way out — this reclamation was added for review finding 62, after one machine held 531 abandoned trees.
- Codex's quota reading is read out of exactly those lane homes, so `verify --live` is the one command that can produce a fresh reading on demand, and it currently destroys its own evidence.
- A dispatcher gate that cannot get a trustworthy reading holds every new launch, so with no manual refresh there is no way back short of running codex by hand.

heading: ## Acceptance criteria
markdown:
- after `spoolway agent verify codex --live` exits, the lane home it created still exists and still holds the rollout the live turn wrote
- a subsequent quota read for that kind resolves from that rollout, so a reading that was stale before the command is fresh after it
- at most one live-check home per kind survives on disk: the newest is kept and every older one is removed, whether the run passed, failed or bailed early
- the scratch git repo under the temp directory is still removed on every exit path, unchanged from today
- a kind whose quota is not read out of a lane home keeps today's behaviour, with its home removed on the way out
- the pruning runs from the `Drop` guard, so an early `?` or `bail!` cleans up the same way an ordinary pass does

heading: ## Context
markdown:
- Every command finds a home-mode project by reading every `~/.spoolway/*/project.toml` and looking for the checkout's path. See `all_workspaces` and `workspace_clone` in `src/repo.rs`.
- `all_workspaces` drops any `project.toml` that fails to read or parse (`toml::from_str(..).ok()?`), without saying so.
- `workspace_clone` returns the first match across an unsorted `read_dir`, so two workspaces listing one path resolve to whichever the filesystem returns first.
- The `dispatcher` field is joined onto the workspace folder with no validation (`home_dir`), although `spoolway-label` is validated against the same escape.
- A clone path that is not valid UTF-8 is recorded with `from_utf8_lossy`, so it can never match again.
- `~/.spoolway/` is shared with every project spoolway 0.6.0 set up. A 0.6.0 repo-mode home holds a `project.toml` too, with only `id` and `root` and no `clones`. `~/.spoolway/` can also hold a legacy home with no `project.toml` at all (such as `~/.spoolway/spoolway/`), and folders that are no home, such as `logs/` and `.dispatcher/`. Today these are told apart from workspaces only because they fail to parse as one.

heading: ## Acceptance criteria
markdown:
- the repro written by the reproduce step fails before the fix and passes after it
- a `project.toml` that cannot be read or parsed is reported by every command that scans workspaces, naming the file, and `init` refuses rather than falling back to repo mode
- a checkout listed more than once, in one workspace or across several, is an error naming every file and entry
- a `dispatcher` value that is not one plain name is refused, and a clone path that is not valid UTF-8 is refused at `init` rather than stored lossily
- only a file that is a workspace is reported: one with a `clones` key, or one beside a `config/` or `dispatchers/` folder. A 0.6.0 repo-mode home (`id` and `root`, no `clones`), a legacy home with no `project.toml`, and folders such as `logs/` are skipped silently, as they are today
- a `~/.spoolway/` holding homes written by spoolway 0.6.0 (`scripts/e2e/fixtures/0.6.0/` or a real 0.6.0 install) produces no new error or warning from any command, in repo mode or home mode; a test covers this

heading: ## Context
markdown:
- `join_workspace` in `src/repo.rs` reads `project.toml`, changes it and writes it back, with no lock.
- `init` calls `create_workspace` or `join_workspace`, and `bind`, before `Answers::gather` checks or asks anything (`src/commands/init.rs`). In repo mode, a bad answer still stamps `.git` and creates a home.
- A join creates the `dispatchers/<name>` folder first, then writes `project.toml`.
- `init --setup home` checks for a tracked `.spoolway/` only on the branch checked out now. `Repo::root` already knows the "`.spoolway/` is not on this branch" case.

heading: ## Acceptance criteria
markdown:
- the repro written by the reproduce step fails before the fix and passes after it
- writes to a workspace's `project.toml` hold a lock, so concurrent joins all end up listed
- `init` validates every flag and gathers every answer before it creates, joins or binds anything, in both modes
- a failed join removes the dispatcher folder it created, names the path in its error, and a join into a workspace with no `config/` is refused
- `init --setup home` is refused when the repository tracks `.spoolway/` on its default branch, naming that branch
- a repeat `init` in a project spoolway 0.6.0 set up (a repo-mode home with `id` and `root`, and a `.git/spoolway-id` stamp) still succeeds and binds to that same home, and the new lock adds no folder directly under `~/.spoolway/`
